principle: The structured Sequence/rubric problem selects bounded Engines. Engines do not decide their own authority and do not replace the Universal Sequence runtime.

when: source intake or exact text lock
sentence/phrase contains mixed signal, noise, clauses, negation or qualifiers
question/ask has ambiguous real target or scope
routes.purpose: extract declared-end candidate without turning it into hidden intent fact

when: coarse rubric match requires deeper Pyramid address

routes.purpose: bounded analytical reasoning over explicit objects/relations

when: same/different structure must be compared with examples or prior cases
routes.purpose: example-first match, Pyramid memory and Sequence-to-Sequence comparison

when: pattern remains vague, recursive, cross-case or requires deeper reverse/forward exploration
routes.purpose: controlled recursive expansion; each new investigation/retry remains a separate Sequence contract when it executes work

when: multiple local interpretations/results must be combined without losing provenance
routes.purpose: merge bounded return packets; preserve contradictions and source refs
verification, reverse check and proof-debt generation

when: cross-domain priority, governance, permission or conflicting interpretations require arbitration
routes.purpose: meta-governance/arbitration; Meta does not erase lower-level local results

when: approved review changes future pattern/rubric behavior
response must be checked against accumulated evidence and suitability before presentation
routes.purpose: appropriate output gate; output mapping cannot rewrite source truth

routing_laws: One micro-Sequence may activate multiple Engines in parallel or in dependency order.
An Engine request must name its input contract, requested result, scope and return acceptance condition.
Engine result is evidence/output, not execution authority.
META is invoked for meta-governance/conflict/priority, not as a default substitute for local analysis.
RGL recursion cannot become an unbounded in-place loop; executable investigation/repair/retest work receives its own Sequence/Sub-Sequence contract.
ARD may infer; inferred intent/motive remains epistemically typed and reviewable.
Pattern Engines create Pattern Contributions/Candidates, never automatic approved rubrics.
User-approved edit flows through versioned learning write-back before future reuse.
